title: Make the chat/turnStarted reducer idempotent
body:
Mirrors https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/433 into the synced copy of the chat reducer, and adds the VS Code side tests for the overlay behaviour it fixes.

## Why

`ChatStateSubscription` replays every still-pending optimistic action over confirmed state on each confirmed action, and retirement is echo-only. A `chat/turnStarted` that is never echoed is replayed on every delta, and the reducer case rebuilt `activeTurn` with empty `responseParts` each time, wiping streamed content. That is the mechanism behind #332087. #332122 narrows the window by promoting the pending start when a terminal action arrives; this makes the reducer itself safe to replay, which also covers a start replayed after the turn was confirmed complete through a snapshot.

## The synced file

`channels-chat/reducer.ts` is generated by `scripts/sync-agent-host-protocol.ts` and must not be edited by hand, so the change is proposed upstream in https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/433. The hunk here is byte-identical to that change after the sync transformations, so the next sync is a no-op for it. This PR is a draft until the upstream change lands and is synced.

## Tests

- `ChatTurnStarted replayed over the turn it started is a no-op` (fresh start and streaming turn with content; asserts the fixture really has content)
- `ChatTurnStarted for a completed turn is a no-op`
- `ChatTruncated is idempotent` (documents that `reduce(reduce(s,a),a)` equals `reduce(s,a)` for both forms; the stranded-truncation case needs overlay retirement, which is a separate change)
- `stranded optimistic turn start does not reset a confirmed streaming turn` in the subscription tests, exercising `_recomputeOptimistic` exactly as the bug does

Without the guard the two turn-start reducer tests and the subscription test fail. `reducers.test`: 34 passing. `agentSubscription.test`: 61 passing. No new type errors.

Audit of the other thirteen client-dispatchable chat actions: all already idempotent, either guarded on a status the first application leaves behind or pure value assignments.

Part of #333174.

title: Reclaim orphaned agent session data directories
body:
Reclaims agent session data directories that nothing could ever delete, and stops the startup prune from creating more of them.

## Measured

In one session store, 503 of 528 directories held a 65536-byte schema-only `session.db` with zero turns. Across five stores on the same machine, 96% of directories were empty shells.

## Cause

- Every newly registered external session (discovered from a provider's own catalogue rather than created by this host) gets `_initializeExternalSessionReadState`, which writes read state through `openDatabase(...).setMetadata`, and the database creates the directory on that first write. Discovery alone creates a directory per external session.
- `_pruneStaleExternalSessions` unregisters rows older than 30 days but never deletes their data. Once the registry row is gone the directory can never be matched to a session again, and discovery skips re-registering it. That is the leak's closing move.
- `SessionDataService.cleanupOrphanedData` does the right thing and had zero production callers. Its contract also took directory names, which nothing outside the service could produce correctly, since sanitisation and the chat-URI keying live inside it.

## Fix

- The prune deletes the session data of every row it prunes.
- A startup sweep runs behind the prune, handing `cleanupOrphanedData` the registered sessions (as URIs) plus any in-memory and unpersisted chat backings. A directory is kept when it is the session's own, a subagent session of it (`<id>-subagent-<call>`), or a peer chat of it (matched on the base64url session fragment every chat-channel directory carries). `devcontainer-worktree-*` data is never touched.
- A directory whose database carries the chat-backing marker is kept. The marker key moves to a shared constant so the data service can recognise it.

## Guards

The sweep never runs unless the registry enumeration resolves, and never when it lists zero sessions, so a lost or fresh registry cannot wipe a populated store. Any per-directory failure, including failing to open its database, keeps that directory. Matching only ever errs toward keeping.

## Tests

- `prune deletes the session data of every stale external row`
- `startup cleanup sweeps orphaned session data with the registered sessions` (end to end through startup, asserting the exact URI set handed to the sweep)
- `startup cleanup is skipped while the registry is empty`
- `startup cleanup deletes nothing when the registry cannot be enumerated`
- `deletes orphans but keeps known sessions and the data they own` (session, its peer chat, its subagent directory and `devcontainer-worktree-*` survive; the orphan and its peer chat are deleted)
- `keeps the backing session of a chat`

`sessionDataService.test`: 13 passing. `agentService.test`: 409 passing, 0 failing. No new type errors.

## Out of scope

Not creating the directory on discovery at all would need a durable registry default for read state, which changes listing semantics. With the two fixes above the per-external-session database is bounded by registry rows, so it is a cost rather than a leak. Peer-chat directories of a session the user deletes are reclaimed by the next startup sweep rather than at delete time.

Part of #333174.

title: Keep tool attribution across a steering preempt
body:
Keeps tool-call attribution and foreground subagent spawns alive across a steering preempt, so a tool still running when the user steers is completed and rendered rather than left at Running forever.

## Defect

When a steering message preempts a running Claude turn, the SDK emits a `result` for the preempted turn even though the protocol turn is not over. The pipeline already treats that as an intermediate result and defers `ChatTurnComplete` until the queue is drained. The mapper did not: `mapResult` cleared the `tool_use_id` attribution map and drained foreground subagent spawns on every `result`, intermediate ones included. A tool call still in flight when the steer landed lost its attribution, so its later `tool_result` hit the unknown-id path and produced no `ChatToolCallComplete`. The tool stayed Running indefinitely, and any subagent it had spawned vanished from the registry, so `subagent_started` was never emitted and the inner signals were buffered forever.

## Fix

Turn-end cleanup belongs to the component that knows when the protocol turn ends. `mapResult` now maps usage and error signals only. The router exposes `clearPendingTurnState`, and the pipeline calls it in the same branch that fires `ChatTurnComplete`, so attribution is dropped exactly once, on the final result. Abort and dispose paths are unchanged in practice: no `result` is routed after an abort, and stale entries are still dropped on the next turn's final result with the existing orphan warnings.

## Tests

Mapper:
- `result keeps a pending tool_use so a tool_result that lands after a steering preempt still completes it`
- `result keeps a foreground subagent spawn in the registry`
- `clearPendingToolCalls drains tool_use entries that never received a tool_result and warns once per orphan`

Pipeline, driven through the real queue and router:
- `intermediate result during steering keeps tool-call attribution so a later tool_result still completes the tool`
- `intermediate result during steering keeps the foreground subagent spawn so inner content still announces subagent_started`
- `final result drops pending tool-call attribution so a late tool_result is treated as unknown`

The first two in each group fail without the fix and pass with it. Sibling suites (pipeline, router, tool-call registry, subagent registry and signals, prompt queue, replay mapper) all pass. No new type errors.

Part of #333174.

title: Chat: model disappears between enumeration and chat.open
body:
A model can be reported as available by `vscode.lm.selectChatModels`, but an immediately following `workbench.action.chat.open` call using that same model selector can fail with `No language models found matching selector`. This makes model availability internally inconsistent and forces callers to retry a model that VS Code just reported as registered.


**Reproduction and observed behavior**

1. Call `vscode.lm.selectChatModels` and observe the target model in the returned list.
2. Immediately invoke `workbench.action.chat.open` with the matching `{ vendor, id }` selector.
3. Intermittently, the command fails with `No language models found matching selector`.
4. Retrying the same command shortly afterward succeeds without changing the selector.
